intent: Share a right-to-left or left-to-right reading direction with the Base UI-backed kit components in a subtree that read it.
typical_uses: Once near the root of an application, or of the subtree, that renders a right-to-left language

dont_use_when.situation: An application that only renders left-to-right

instead.note: With no DirectionProvider mounted, `useDirection()` and every primitive reading it fall back to `ltr`.

dont_use_when.situation: Setting the browser's own text direction for layout and bidirectional text

instead.target: the `dir` attribute on the application's own root element
instead.note: DirectionProvider sets no `dir` attribute anywhere; it only shares a value through context, which a root element can read with `useDirection()` to set `dir` itself.

invariants.text: DirectionProvider renders no DOM element and sets no attribute; it only provides context to the components below it.

Base UI primitives that read the direction context (among them the keyboard navigation of composite lists and menus, the slider, the scroll area's scrollbar and the placement of anchored popups) take the `direction` of the nearest DirectionProvider above them, and `ltr` with none.

rtl.by: direction.test.tsx asserts that useDirection() returns "rtl" under <DirectionProvider direction="rtl"> and "ltr" with no provider mounted; the primitive's DirectionProvider provides that value through context and nothing else

children.states: children is any React content; every Base UI primitive inside it, at any depth, reads the direction
children.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more; the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

good.title: A right-to-left application whose root element also carries dir
good.code:
function App() { const direction = useDirection(); return
{content}
; }

bad.title: A dir prop on the provider
bad.why: The prop is `direction`; DirectionProvider renders no element, so a `dir` it is given reaches no DOM node and the direction stays `ltr`.

companions.description: Reads the `direction` of the nearest DirectionProvider, or `ltr` with none mounted.
The type of `direction` and of the value useDirection returns.
